policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV coordinates the two infinitives, 'pressed upon him and heard the word of God'; the RP genitive article would give a purpose clause ('to hear'), which the ASV does not render.
Pure word order within the noun phrase; both readings yield ASV 'two boats'.
Word order only; both readings yield 'had gone out of them'.
ASV 'were washing their nets' renders the imperfect ἔπλυνον; the RP aorist ἀπέπλυναν would give a simple past 'washed'.
The variant is only the article before the proper name; ASV 'which was Simon's' is the same either way.
Conjunction (δέ/καί, both 'And' in ASV) plus word order of 'out of the boat'; English clause order here does not track the Greek.
Article before Σίμων only; ASV 'Simon' is unaffected.
ASV reads 'answered and said, Master' with no 'unto him'; the added αὐτῷ would be rendered.
Article with ὅλης νυκτός only; ASV 'all night' either way.
ASV 'I will let down the nets' is plural, matching τὰ δίκτυα against the RP singular τὸ δίκτυον.
Alternative imperfect forms of the same verb; both give ASV 'were breaking'.
ASV 'their nets were breaking' is plural, matching τὰ δίκτυα against the RP singular τὸ δίκτυον.
Added article only; ASV 'their partners' is the same either way.
The relative differs only in antecedent (fishes vs. draught); ASV 'the draught of the fishes which they had taken' leaves the antecedent open in English.
Presence of the article before the name; ASV 'Jesus' is unaffected. The verse notes concern the English name Jacob and a gloss on 'catch men', not this unit.
πάντα and ἅπαντα are equivalent; ASV 'all' either way.
καί and δέ are both rendered 'and' in ASV 'and when he saw Jesus'; the participle is identical.
εἰπών and λέγων are both rendered 'saying'.
ASV 'to be healed of their infirmities' has no agent phrase; the RP addition ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ would be rendered 'by him'.
The mapped note gives the ASV text as 'Greek that he should heal' with 'that he should heal them' only as the marginal alternative, so the text renders αὐτόν, not αὐτούς.
ASV 'to lay him before him' carries over the object of the preceding 'to bring him in', which English requires with or without the Greek pronoun.
ASV 'he said, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee' has no 'unto him'; the RP addition αὐτῷ would be rendered.
Word order only; ASV 'forgive sins' either way.
Alternative imperative forms of the same verb; ASV 'Arise' either way.
Word order only; ASV 'the Son of man hath authority' either way.
Alternative imperative forms of the same verb; ASV 'Arise' either way.
πάντα and ἅπαντα are equivalent; ASV 'all' either way.
ASV 'followed him' is a simple past that renders either the imperfect or the aorist here.
Word order only; ASV 'a great multitude of publicans' either way.
ASV 'the Pharisees and their scribes' names the Pharisees first, matching the base order; RP puts the scribes first.
ASV frames the saying as a statement, 'The disciples of John fast often'; the Treg/RP Διὰ τί would make it a question, 'Why do the disciples of John fast?'
ASV 'And Jesus said unto them' names Jesus without italics, so the subject stands in the Greek rather than being supplied.
Aorist and present infinitive of the same verb; ASV 'fast' either way.
ASV 'rendeth a piece from a new garment' renders the preposition ἀπό; the RP reading has a bare genitive, 'a piece of a new garment'.
ASV has two verbs, 'rendeth ... and putteth', rendering σχίσας alongside ἐπιβάλλει; RP omits the participle and has only 'putteth'.
ASV 'else he will rend the new' is future, matching σχίσει against the RP present σχίζει.
ASV 'the piece from the new will not agree with the old' has both the expressed subject τὸ ἐπίβλημα and the future verb; RP has the bare present συμφωνεῖ with no subject noun.
Word order and article only; ASV 'the new wine' either way.
ASV ends the verse at 'must be put into fresh wine-skins'; the Treg/RP addition 'and both are preserved' is absent.
ASV opens the verse 'And no man having drunk old wine', rendering the connective καί that WH omits.
ASV 'desireth new' has no 'straightway'; the RP addition εὐθέως would be rendered.
ASV text reads 'The old is good' (χρηστός), with the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read better' relegating the comparative χρηστότερος to the margin.
